findings.title: The per-account cap gate's use of the per-tick resolved map is asserted by nothing: reverting it to the platform constant leaves all 61 cases green, and lets a sub-default-capped account release past its configured cap
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Two independent survivors on an EXECUTED line (rt-11 M10, rt-12 M15). Not equivalent and not an unexecuted branch: line 1305 runs for every candidate account in almost every case, and only the VALUE differs. Reachable and meaningful in production — an account configured at 5 with 3 attempts today passes the scan arm (3 < 5), so the gate is what bounds it; under the mutant `counters.account` becomes 10 - 3 = 7 instead of 5 - 3 = 2, and with >= 3 rendered rows in the batch the account releases up to 7 and ends the day at 10 attempts against a configured cap of 5 — a silent breach of the enforced cap, and the exact 'arm and gate disagree about one account's number' failure the intake's third invariant names. Every existing fixture is blind to it because each one has at most ONE rendered row available, so the row supply, not the counter, bounds `released`. Fix: one case seeding a configured cap of 2 with 0 attempts and >= 3 rendered rows in a single batch, asserting released === 2 and withheldByReason.account_cap >= 1; that kills both M10 and M15.

findings.title: The new 'lockstep pin' cannot fail on the drift it exists to catch, and its only live assertion is an array ORDER its own docstring disclaims
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Proven in both directions. M12 removed SubscriptionStatus.TRIALING from FULL_ACCESS_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES — verbatim the drift the case's own comment names ('a status admitted by one and refused by the other') — and this case PASSED; the kill came from three pre-existing cases. M12b reordered the array to [TRIALING, ACTIVE], a behaviour-preserving edit, and this case was the SOLE failure of 18, while src/lib/shared/subscription-status.ts:64 states 'Order is `active` then `trialing` and is not meaningful'. Both of its assertions compare the array against a list derived from `subscriptionGrantsFullAccess`, which is itself implemented over that same array (subscription-status.ts:85) — true by construction for any array of canonical statuses in enum order. This is a Duty-2 order assertion with no contract AND a vacuous claim cited in the branch's evidence as the lockstep guarantee. Fix: assert the members against a literal expectation and drop the order coupling (`expect(new Set(FULL_ACCESS_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES)).toEqual(new Set([SubscriptionStatus.ACTIVE, SubscriptionStatus.TRIALING]))`), and delete the predicate-derived comparison rather than keeping a tautology.

findings.title: The restored per-account gate read `readAccountDailySendCap` has an entirely unpinned WHERE clause: dropping its row-identity predicate and dropping its tenant scope each leave 66/66 green
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Two independent survivors on a line that executes for every candidate account in almost every case, so neither is an unexecuted branch. M6 (rt2-05) removes `AND location_id IS NULL`; M11 (rt2-06) removes `AND account_id = ${accountId}::uuid`. Neither is equivalent. Under M6 a location-OVERRIDE row — migration 091's per-BUSINESS ceiling, which the CHECK admits — becomes the whole account's gate cap, and with `LIMIT 1` and no `ORDER BY` which override wins is arbitrary; the branch's own new case proves this predicate is load-bearing for the ARM read and says so in its comment, while the identical predicate in the GATE read the same fix restored is asserted by nothing. Under M11 the gate reads SOME other account's dial, which is a cross-tenant read against invariant #8 and nondeterministic for the same reason. Every fixture is blind to both because the cases that seed two policy rows resolve both to 10. Smallest fix: extend `reads the account-default policy row, never a location override` to the PRIMARY account with a releasable batch — a location override of 1 plus an account default of 10 must still release, which kills M6 — and give the foreign account a distinct configured cap so the primary's gate arithmetic can only be right if it read its own row, which kills M11.

findings.title: The new fifth delegating spy sits outside the suite's `beforeEach` re-arm contract, and its `mockImplementationOnce` survives `vi.clearAllMocks()`, so an unconsumed override would leak into the next case
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured against the installed spy implementation, not assumed: `node_modules/.pnpm/@vitest+spy@4.1.7/node_modules/@vitest/spy/dist/index.js:142-157` shows `mockClear()` resetting only `state.calls/contexts/instances/invocationCallOrder/results/settledResults`, while `config.onceMockImplementations = []` happens only in `mockReset()`. `vi.clearAllMocks()` calls `mockClear`, so a `mockImplementationOnce` that is never consumed stays queued for every later case in the file. The other four delegating spies are re-armed from `vi.importActual` in `beforeEach` (lines 886-903), which would overwrite a leaked base implementation; `countAccountDispatchAttemptsToday` is deliberately absent from that list, so nothing re-arms it. The leak is LATENT today — the new lapse case is the only override and it is consumed, because `runAccountArm` reaches the counter for the single seeded account — which is why this is P2 and not P1. Two related drifts: the `beforeEach` comment still says "this file `vi.mock`s all four modules" when there are now five delegating mocks, and `getMockImplementation()!` would throw rather than mislead if the base implementation were ever cleared, which is the safe direction. An order-shuffle probe (`--sequence.shuffle.tests --sequence.seed=424242`) also stayed 66/66, but the JSON reporter emits declaration order so I could not confirm the flag took effect; that probe is recorded as unconfirmed rather than as evidence.

It is unreachable while migration 074:75-77's partial unique index holds — which is why rt2-07 is `equivalent` and not a coverage gap — but if that index were ever dropped or diverged between the two Supabase projects, every release tick would fail for as long as the duplicate row existed, and `docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md` has no rule row for the release cycle to surface it. The diff adds no `logger.*`, `captureException` or Sentry signal, so nothing pages. Recorded rather than raised as P1 because the missing runbook coverage for this phase is PRE-EXISTING and the branch neither creates nor worsens it; what is new is only the blast radius of one more unreachable throw.
